items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: Now we had some very good fellas, a fella like Buddy B.T. He had a very good, he had a good talent, a good gift like that.

ctx.x: The leader of the band wouldn't dictate what to do.

I mean… Oh, he couldn't dictate because sometimes you'd have fellas in there on making up those things, improvising, you see, more better than him. But, so before I lead the band, that was his job. Now we had some very good fellas, a fella like Buddy B.T. He had a very good, he had a good talent, a good gift like that. Well, he would always have, even like trombone parts, anything like that.
He'd help you with that? Yeah.

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-11
items.q: He left me about three or four times. I fell down. That's how Amos got with me once and Mutt got with me once when he left. I said, Buddy Bacique got in there.

ctx.x: Oh, Solistan was in my lifetime playing first. You see, Solistan leaving my band and I didn't care where he would go, I'd always have open for him. When he come back, well he got ready to come back to the band and they all well understood that. They never did try to keep them out. You know, if he got out of the job he used to come right on back. But we started together and both of us was coming to boys and I kept the band going. He used to come right on back whenever he got ready. He left me about three or four…
Could you give me that picture of Thomas' man?
